x-e-e2-01.title: Match the park sign and Tom's plan
x-e-e2-01.goal: Compare the lines of the sign with Tom's plan one by one, find the parts that don't match, and tell him in English.
x-e-e2-01.material:
The sign at the park entrance (written in words only, no picture):

Sun Park
Open: 7 a.m. - 6 p.m.
No bikes.
Dogs OK.

Your friend Tom said, "I will go to Sun Park with my dog and my bike at 7 p.m.!"
x-e-e2-01.thinking.0: Compare each line of the sign with one part of the plan
x-e-e2-01.thinking.1: Judge using a.m./p.m. times as evidence
x-e-e2-01.thinking.2: Tell apart what is a problem and what is fine
x-e-e2-01.prereq.1: Easy words like open, bike, dog
x-e-e2-01.s.s1.prompt: Choose every part of Tom's plan that doesn't match the sign.
x-e-e2-01.s.s1.hint.0: Split Tom's plan into four pieces, 'dog', 'bike', 'time', and 'place', and match each one with the lines of the sign.
x-e-e2-01.s.s1.hint.1: Look at which side a.m. and p.m. are attached to in the 'Open' line.
x-e-e2-01.s.s1.r.a: Reread what the 'Dogs OK.' line says about dogs.
x-e-e2-01.s.s1.r.b: Put the 'No bikes.' line and Tom's plan side by side and compare. This part goes against the sign.
x-e-e2-01.s.s1.r.c: Compare the a.m./p.m. next to the numbers in the Open line with Tom's time. This part also goes against the sign.
x-e-e2-01.s.s1.r.d: The park's name is the same as the top line of the sign.
x-e-e2-01.s.s1.explain: The sign says no bikes (No bikes) and the gate closes at 6 p.m. Tom said he will bring a bike and go at 7 p.m., so those two parts don't match. Dogs are OK and the park name is the same.
x-e-e2-01.s.s2.prompt: Answer Tom in English in one or two sentences. Tell him two things in his plan that won't work.
x-e-e2-01.s.s2.hint.0: First write one problem in one sentence.
x-e-e2-01.s.s2.hint.1: Write the other problem in the second sentence, and include a time or a word from the sign.
x-e-e2-01.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Did you mention both the bike problem and the time problem?
x-e-e2-01.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Can you say which line of the sign each of your reasons comes from?
x-e-e2-01.s.s2.selfAssess.2: Did you avoid mixing up that the dog is fine? (optional)
x-e-e2-01.s.s2.modelNote.1: A good answer that even suggests another time.

x-e-e2-02.title: Find and fix the line with the wrong meeting time

x-e-e2-02.material: Jen and Sam are talking by text.
x-e-e2-02.thinking.0: Compare earlier lines of information with later lines
x-e-e2-02.thinking.1: Find the line where the error first appears
x-e-e2-02.s.s1.prompt: Choose the first wrong line in the conversation, the one that doesn't match what an earlier line says.
x-e-e2-02.s.s1.hint.0: Find in line 2 until when Sam can't come.
x-e-e2-02.s.s1.hint.1: Compare the time in each line with that time, one by one.
x-e-e2-02.s.s1.explain: In line 2, Sam said piano class lasts until 4:30. The 4:15 in line 3 is before the class ends, so it doesn't match. Line 4 just repeats line 3, so the place where the error first appears is line 3.
x-e-e2-02.s.s2.prompt: Fix Jen's line 3 and write it again in English, with a time Sam can come.
x-e-e2-02.s.s2.hint.0: Choose a time later than the time Sam's class ends.
x-e-e2-02.s.s2.hint.1: You can keep 'OK. Let's meet at ...' and change just the time.
x-e-e2-02.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Is the time you wrote later than 4:30?
x-e-e2-02.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Did you think about the time Sam needs to get to the park after class? (optional)
x-e-e2-02.s.s2.modelNote.1: An answer that also thinks about travel time after class.

x-e-e2-03.title: Who is Max? Changing your thinking as clues increase
x-e-e2-03.topic: Clues about time, place, and people
x-e-e2-03.goal: Read the conversation one more line at a time, change your guess about 'who Max is', and write a new clue yourself.
x-e-e2-03.material: The lines heard in a park are shown one line at a time. Think about who the Max in the story is.
x-e-e2-03.thinking.0: Judge again each time a new clue appears
x-e-e2-03.thinking.1: Accept that your first guess may be wrong
x-e-e2-03.thinking.2: Make a line that works as a clue yourself
x-e-e2-03.prereq.0: Easy words like Come here, Sit, Thank you
x-e-e2-03.s.s1.prompt: Read one line at a time and decide your own thought about 'Who might Max be?' As clues increase, your thought may change.
x-e-e2-03.s.s1.hint.0: Check whether your guess fits all the lines so far.
x-e-e2-03.s.s1.hint.1: First compare whether the new line fits your earlier guess.
x-e-e2-03.s.s1.st.0.info: First line: "Come here, Max! Good boy!"
x-e-e2-03.s.s1.st.0.ask: Who is Max most likely to be? Choose the most plausible one.
x-e-e2-03.s.s1.st.0.after: From one line, either a dog or a child is possible. There is not enough clue to settle on one.
x-e-e2-03.s.s1.st.0.r.a: 'Good boy' can be said to either a dog or a child. One line alone can't decide it, but a dog is a reasonable guess.
x-e-e2-03.s.s1.st.0.r.b: These words are also used for children. One line alone doesn't tell them apart from a dog.
x-e-e2-03.s.s1.st.0.r.c: You don't say 'Good boy' to a teacher. These words are usually said to a young child or an animal.
x-e-e2-03.s.s1.st.1.info: Second line: "Sit! Take the ball, Max! Run!"
x-e-e2-03.s.s1.st.1.ask: Now who is Max most likely to be?
x-e-e2-03.s.s1.st.1.after: Because of 'Sit!' and playing with a ball, the dog has become more plausible. The chance that it is a child hasn't completely disappeared.
x-e-e2-03.s.s1.st.1.r.a: A child can also catch a ball in a game. It is possible, but together with 'Sit!', the dog seems more natural.
x-e-e2-03.s.s1.st.1.r.b: You don't say words telling someone to take a ball to a teacher.
x-e-e2-03.s.s1.st.1.r.c: 'Sit!' and throwing a ball are games people often play with dogs.
x-e-e2-03.s.s1.st.2.info: Third line: Max speaks. "Thank you, Dad! I like this game."
x-e-e2-03.s.s1.st.2.ask: After reading up to this line, who is Max most likely to be?
x-e-e2-03.s.s1.st.2.after: Max, who is speaking, thanks Dad, so Max is a child. The earlier 'Sit!' game can be seen as a game played with a child.
x-e-e2-03.s.s1.st.2.r.a: A dog can't say 'Thank you, Dad!' This line doesn't fit the earlier guess.
x-e-e2-03.s.s1.st.2.r.b: There is no clue that the person saying 'Thank you' to Dad is a teacher.
x-e-e2-03.s.s1.st.2.r.c: He speaks to Dad and says he likes the game, so the earlier game scene is also explained.
x-e-e2-03.s.s1.reflect: Even if you first guessed a dog, it is reasonable to change your thinking according to the new clue (Max speaks). A guess settled on from just one line can change in front of a new clue.
x-e-e2-03.s.s2.prompt: In a new conversation, you want it to be clear that Max is a 'dog.' Write one English line that includes Max.
x-e-e2-03.s.s2.hint.0: Think of things done with a dog or sounds a dog makes.
x-e-e2-03.s.s2.hint.1: Put the name Max and that clue together in one sentence.
x-e-e2-03.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Which word in my line shows that it is a dog?
x-e-e2-03.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Is that word one that could be used for a child too?
x-e-e2-03.s.s2.modelNote.1: A bone is a clue for a dog.

x-e-e2-04.title: Find the start time for a 30-minute swim using the pool sign
x-e-e2-04.topic: Clues about time, place, and people
x-e-e2-04.goal: From a sign with opening hours and a cleaning time, find several start times at which a 30-minute swim is fully possible.
x-e-e2-04.material:
The pool sign (written in words only, no picture):

City Pool
Open: 2:00 p.m. - 5:00 p.m.
Closed for cleaning: 3:00 - 3:30 p.m.
One swim: 30 minutes

You and a friend want to swim once in the afternoon for 30 minutes without stopping. The pool must not close before the swim is over.
x-e-e2-04.thinking.0: Find a time that meets several time conditions at once
x-e-e2-04.thinking.1: Think about the end time too
x-e-e2-04.s.s1.prompt: What if you start swimming at 2:45?
x-e-e2-04.s.s1.hint.0: First calculate the time the swim ends.
x-e-e2-04.s.s1.hint.1: Check whether the end time falls inside the cleaning time (3:00-3:30).
x-e-e2-04.s.s1.o.a: Impossible. At 3:15 you are still swimming, but it is cleaning time
x-e-e2-04.s.s1.r.a: This judgment looks at the condition that there is no break during the 30 minutes together with the cleaning time.
x-e-e2-04.s.s1.o.b: Possible. Because it starts before cleaning begins at 3:00
x-e-e2-04.s.s1.r.b: You only looked at the start time. You also have to check what time it is after 30 minutes pass.
x-e-e2-04.s.s1.o.c: Impossible. Because it is earlier than 2:00 when the doors open
x-e-e2-04.s.s1.r.c: 2:45 is later than 2:00, so it is after opening. Compare the opening time and the closing time again.
x-e-e2-04.s.s1.explain: If you start at 2:45, you finish at 3:15. 3:00-3:30 is cleaning time, so the pool closes while you are swimming, which makes it impossible.
x-e-e2-04.s.s2.prompt: Make two different times at which you can start a 30-minute swim. (p.m. h o'clock m minutes)
x-e-e2-04.s.s2.hint.0: Also check the end time, which is the start time plus 30 minutes.
x-e-e2-04.s.s2.hint.1: There are two ways: finish before the cleaning time, or start after cleaning ends.
x-e-e2-04.s.s2.fail.c1: Write the hour as an integer from 1 to 5 and the minute as an integer from 0 to 59.
x-e-e2-04.s.s2.ok.c2: The swim ends while the pool is open.
x-e-e2-04.s.s2.fail.c2: You would start earlier than 2:00, or end up swimming past 5:00.
x-e-e2-04.s.s2.ok.c3: It does not overlap with the cleaning time.
x-e-e2-04.s.s2.fail.c3: The swimming time overlaps with the cleaning time (3:00-3:30).
x-e-e2-04.s.s2.explain: The possible starts are 2:00-2:30 (finishing by 3:00) and 3:30-4:30 (finishing by 5:00). For example, 2:00 and 4:00 work, but 3:00 overlaps with cleaning and 4:45 goes past 5:00, so they don't work.

x-e-e2-05.title: Where is 'Two tickets, please.'? Judging whether the information is enough
x-e-e2-05.topic: Clues about time, place, and people
x-e-e2-05.goal: Judge whether you can decide the place from two overheard lines alone, and choose the extra clue that separates the places.
x-e-e2-05.material:
You overheard what a man and a ticket clerk said. They did not say where it is.

Man: Two tickets, please.
Clerk: Here you are. The show starts at 7:00.
x-e-e2-05.thinking.0: Judge whether the information is enough
x-e-e2-05.thinking.2: Choose the clue that separates the candidates
x-e-e2-05.prereq.0: Easy words like ticket, show, movie, popcorn
x-e-e2-05.s.s1.prompt: Can you decide on one place from these two lines alone?
x-e-e2-05.s.s1.hint.0: Think of two or three places where these two lines could be said.
x-e-e2-05.s.s1.hint.1: Think about whether the place each choice names fits both lines.
x-e-e2-05.s.s1.o.a: We can't decide. Many places are possible, such as a cinema or a concert hall
x-e-e2-05.s.s1.r.a: 'Show' and ticket can be used at several places.
x-e-e2-05.s.s1.o.b: It is a cinema. Because a ticket came up
x-e-e2-05.s.s1.r.b: Ticket also comes up at places other than a cinema, such as a concert hall, a zoo, or a train station.
x-e-e2-05.s.s1.o.c: It is a train station. Because it leaves at 7:00
x-e-e2-05.s.s1.r.c: A train is usually called a 'train', not a 'show'. The evidence is weak.
x-e-e2-05.s.s1.explain: Ticket and show are words used at many places, such as a cinema or a concert hall. It is hard to settle on one from just two lines.
x-e-e2-05.s.s2.prompt: Choose all the extra lines that separate whether the place is a 'cinema' or a 'concert hall'.
x-e-e2-05.s.s2.hint.0: Put each line into both the cinema and the concert hall, and cross out a line that fits both.
x-e-e2-05.s.s2.hint.1: Check whether the remaining lines fit only one of them better.
x-e-e2-05.s.s2.r.a: Popcorn is a food commonly bought at a cinema. It can be a clue that sets it apart from a concert hall.
x-e-e2-05.s.s2.r.b: Both a cinema and a concert hall have rows of seats. These words don't separate the two.
x-e-e2-05.s.s2.r.c: Screen (a display) is a word that matters more at a cinema than at a concert hall. It can be a clue that splits the two.
x-e-e2-05.s.s2.r.d: Being told to be quiet can be heard at both places.
x-e-e2-05.s.s2.explain: Words that fit both candidates (rows of seats, being quiet) don't separate the places. Popcorn and screen are clues closer to a cinema. But it may be hard to settle it completely with just one line.
